podcast.body: This number one hit by Outcast was released in the early 2000s. It was mentioned as a culturally relevant and commercially successful song that had a much longer legacy and stronger Spotify streams compared to U2's "Walk On," which won Record of the Year at the 2002 Grammys over "Ms. Jackson." "Also, at the 2002 Grammys, Walk On beat a pair of number one hits, fallen by Alicia Keys. And Ms. Jackson by Outcast."

podcast.body: This song became Outcast's first blockbuster pop single, topping both the Hot 100 and the R&B chart in the winter of 2001. Contrary to initial belief, it was not about Janet Jackson, though Outcast would sometimes tease audiences live by having their DJ drop a line from Janet's 1986 hit "Nasty." The song was indirectly about Andre's former partner Erica Badu, with whom he had a child, but was directly an apology to Badu's mother, with whom Andre reportedly had an altercation. The song features a recurring piano line borrowed from opera composer Richard Wagner's famed "Bridal Chorus" (The Wedding March), used cleverly in a song about a man refusing to settle down. "The song is an apology for letting down the mother of your child."
